content.title: Inside Rory McIlroy's stunning £16m mansion with recording studio and nine bathrooms
content.text: Despite recently moving into the newly-built mansion in the UK, Ryder Cup star Rory McIlroy has kept his luxurious Florida home, which is now worth twice what he paid for itWhatever happens at the Ryder Cup over the next couple of days, Rory McIlroy and his family will have a luxurious home to return to.As the Masters champion, McIlroy is Team Europe's on-course leader as they look to retain the trophy they took back from Team USA in Rome two years ago. The Northern Irishman has amassed phenomenal wealth from his golfing exploits, and he looks to have spent it wisely, judging by one of the homes he shares with wife Erica Stoll and daughter Poppy.Like many of the European team, McIlroy resides in Florida for much of the year while also having homes in California and Surrey. His Florida pad sits inside the private members' Bear's Club in Jupiter, founded by golf legend Jack Nicklaus (nicknamed the Golden Bear) in 1999.McIlroy moved into the mansion, previously owned by fellow golf star Ernie Els, in 2017, paying around £8million. Due to surging property prices in the sought-after area and upgrades since then, it is now believed to be worth double that amount.With nine bedrooms and 10 bathrooms, the property occupies 2.4 acres of land. Among the luxuries it boasts are an infinity pool, a games room, a tennis court, a home theatre, a state-of-the-art gym and even a recording studio. I have an American wife. I live in America. Honestly, I enjoy it here more. The way of life is easier. The weather. The convenience.”However, he will now spend more time in the UK, having recently moved into a stunning property in Surrey, which he has built to escape the extreme summer heat in Florida.The property, situated in an exclusive celebrity-filled area, is conveniently located close to London and Heathrow Airport, while the illustrious Wentworth Golf Club is next door.Discussing the new house earlier this year, he told the Telegraph: “Straight after Augusta, we travelled over to see the house as it was going through the finishing touches.
